rules.cwe_name: Reliance on Undefined, Unspecified, or Implementation-Defined Behavior
rules.description: If an HTML element has two attributes with the same name but different values, its behavior may be browser-dependent.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
rules.description: Modifying an object obtained via a user-controlled property name may lead to accidental mutation of the built-in Object prototype, and possibly escalate to remote code execution or cross-site scripting.

rules.cwe_name: Use of Potentially Dangerous Function
rules.description: DOM functions that act like 'eval' and execute strings as code are dangerous and impede program analysis and understanding. Consequently, they should not be used.

rules.cwe_name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')
rules.description: A 'for' loop that increments its loop variable but checks it against a lower bound, or decrements its loop variable but checks it against an upper bound, will either stop iterating immediately or keep iterating indefinitely, and is usually indicative of a typo.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
rules.description: Using uncontrolled stored values in HTML allows for a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability.

rules.cwe_name: Incorrect Authorization
rules.description: An authorization check exists but evaluates access incorrectly.

rules.cwe_name: Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs
rules.description: Checking for the "javascript:" URL scheme without also checking for "vbscript:" and "data:" suggests a logic error or even a security vulnerability.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Input Validation
rules.description: Using indexOf to implement endsWith functionality is error-prone if the -1 case is not explicitly handled.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS)
rules.description: Matching HTML tags using regular expressions is hard to do right, and can easily lead to security issues.

rules.cwe_name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
rules.description: Making a client-to-server request with user-controlled data in the URL allows a request forgery attack against the client.
